title: Case: Succession planning at TechSoft GmbH
text: TechSoft GmbH develops software for banks and investment firms. Its clients are mainly in Frankfurt, its headquarters in a tech hub just outside the city. The company is 35 years old, employs about 150 people, has been listed for ten years and is known for innovative yet reliable solutions.

The CEO wants a succession plan for key employees over the next three years. Many senior managers have been with the firm since its founding and will retire soon, but few new people were hired to prepare for this.

Chief Financial Officer: she retires within a year and nobody inside is ready to replace her. Beyond financial expertise she knows the company's financial history in depth and is the CEO's most trusted advisor on strategic decisions. A strong successor who fits the role and the firm is vital for investor confidence and financial stability.

Head of Product Development: he joined 30 years ago as a junior developer and rose through senior developer, project manager and department lead, earning a bachelor's and a master's degree in business administration in evening classes. He sits on the executive team, the CEO values his views, and his consistent performance, fair leadership and deep knowledge of TechSoft's software architecture make him highly respected. The department recently hired several young professionals with strong technical skills; five of them have shown the ambition and potential to take over his role within three years.
